sources.entry: cachetools - Extensible memoizing collections and decorators.

summary.one_liner: cachetools is a Python library providing memoizing collections (bounded caches with various eviction algorithms) and decorators, including variants of functools' lru_cache.
summary.what_it_does: The module offers multiple cache classes, each implementing a different cache algorithm, all behaving as mutable mappings of a fixed maximum size that discard items when full. It provides a @cached decorator that memoizes function calls using a chosen cache object, and the README's examples show LRUCache and TTLCache (time-to-live) usage. The README describes a cache-algorithm-based design where the cache decides which item(s) to evict when adding would exceed maxsize. It also links to related projects that add asyncio support and other cache extensions. Installation is via pip from PyPI.
use_cases: memoize expensive function calls in Python
cache web API or weather lookups with an expiry time
limit memory use of an in-process cache
use least-recently-used eviction for a dictionary-like cache
add caching to methods with a decorator
notable: Cache classes built on different eviction algorithms such as LRU and TTL, all with a fixed maxsize
@cached decorator that works with any of the provided cache objects
Variants of the standard library's lru_cache
Related projects listed for asyncio integration and persistent caches
caveats: README does not state platform or Python version requirements
README does not describe the full set of cache classes beyond the examples
